svg.title: macOS · Import from Device · complete · 460×520
svg.desc: Mirrors Remote/ImportWindow.swift (done phase) over AppModel.commitIncoming. Reached when the server's `transferDone` frame lands, which it only sends after every chunk has been accepted by the connection. The install itself is the source-agnostic half of the archive importer, lifted out for this: AppModel.installStagedProject reads the staged tree's `project.json`, asks the duplicate question if the library already holds this project (matched on the manifest id against project ids AND CaptureProject.importedFromID), mints fresh UUIDs for the capture and every blend — folder names and lookups key on them, so reusing the originals would collide with the source device's own library — renames `source/`, `blends/` and `notes/` into place, re-keys the blends and writes library.json. Because the staging folder is on the library's own volume, all of that is renames rather than copies. Whichever tree it came from, a `.lapse` archive or the network, it is the same job from here — the two paths differ only in how the tree got there. Installs are serialised against the archive importer (one writer of library.json, and the duplicate question has one home: the existing import sheet, which is why it is borrowed for the few seconds this takes). "Import another" returns to the browse list keeping the link; "Done" (⏎) closes the window, and closing it disconnects and stops browsing — an in-flight pull would otherwise keep a phone's radio and this Mac's disk busy with nowhere to report it. THE TRANSFER NEVER DELETED ANYTHING ON THE OTHER DEVICE: it is a copy, in both directions, always. The serving side is read-only by construction — someone who wants the space back deletes the project themselves, on the device, having seen it arrive. Verified 2026-08-27: this is a screenshot of a real project moving simulator→Mac and landing in the library.

g.text: “Sunset over harbour” was added to your library.
